history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: CSV row 2295 ('Jagannath Temple, Banjara Hills', Hyderabad, Telangana) is a confirmed duplicate of seq 978 ('Jagannath Temple', Hyderabad - id jagannath-temple-banjara-hills-hyderabad). Both rows refer to the same temple: the modern Jagannath Temple on Road No. 12, Banjara Hills (Bhavani Nagar), Hyderabad, built by the Kalinga Cultural Trust of Hyderabad (the city's Oriya community) and opened in March 2009. Deduplicate downstream; keep seq 978 as the primary record. (Identity note: Mahesh's brief for this batch names 'the modern Jagannath temple (2009)', matching seq 978 exactly.) The red-sandstone complex spreads over about 10.7 acres and is 72 ft high (compared to Puri's 214 ft); it replicates the Puri plan with Garbha Gruha, Jagan Mohan, dancing hall and Bhoga Mandap, with mythological murals carved on the boundary walls. The main deities - Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra - are wooden idols like those at Puri; the five sub-shrine deities are stone. The complex also has the 'Chakadola' light-and-sound show on the emergence of the Jagannath cult (introduced 2018) and a 3D projection mapping show on weekends. Research carried over from the primary record (seq 978); sources below are those consulted for that record.
